The rulebook

Think in three dimensions.

Two armies. One cube. Your pieces can travel through all eight layers—not just across a board.

♜
Rooks & queens

Slide along straight lines through any of the cube’s three axes. Bishops also travel along 2D and 3D diagonals.

♘
Knight & king

Knights leap in 3D L-shapes. Kings step one cell in any direction. Keep yours safe.

♙
Pawns

White advances toward higher layers; Black toward lower ones. Capture diagonally in the next layer. Reach the far face to promote.

⌗
Explore the cube

Use the layer strip or arrow keys to inspect each 8×8 slice. Click a glowing square to complete a move across layers.

Standard check rules apply. Pawns promote to queens. Castling is not used in Voxel Chess.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 8×8×8 chess game where pieces can move through the cube’s layers.

## Requirements
- Build it now without clarification; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.
- Check the game with screenshots saved as small JPEGs (viewport no wider than 1280px), reading only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Implemented a local pass-and-play game with 8×8×8 layers, 3D movement, layer navigation, move history, captures, undo, check/checkmate, stalemate, and pawn promotion.
- Assumed pawns advance between depth layers; castling is not used.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the game interface, styling, and gameplay logic in `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js`.
- `node --check game.js` passed.
- Chromium loaded the local page and reported 64 board squares and initial White-to-move state.
- Added a layer-track indicator for layers containing legal moves.

### Active
- Validate piece selection and legal movement, including cross-layer moves and undo; investigate why the last browser interaction found no legal move markers.
- Review the latest JPEG screenshot and address any visual or gameplay issues.

### Blocked
- Browser check reported no `.legal-dot` or `.legal-capture` elements after clicking `data-square="0,1,0"`; determine whether the move rendering or test interaction is at fault.

## Next Move
1. Inspect `game.js` selection/move generation and reproduce the empty legal-move result in Chromium.
2. Finish browser interaction checks for cross-layer pawn movement, turn changes, and undo.
3. Review `/tmp/opencode/voxel-latest.jpg` if it exists; recapture a JPEG at ≤1280px if needed.
4. Summarize the finished game and its assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI and rules dialog.
- `style.css`: Responsive visual design and board styling.
- `game.js`: 3D chess rules, move validation, UI state, and interactions.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Chromium remote debugging was started on port `9222`; an interaction probe returned an empty list for legal-move markers after selecting the White pawn at `0,1,0`.
- A PNG screenshot was saved at `/tmp/opencode/voxel-check.png`; JPEG capture was attempted at `/tmp/opencode/voxel-latest.jpg`.

Built a playable 8×8×8 pass-and-play chess game in `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js`.

Pieces can move through the cube’s layers. The game includes legal-move indicators, layer navigation, captures, move history, undo, check/checkmate, stalemate, and pawn promotion. Legal moves on other layers now highlight those layers in the navigation strip.

**Assumptions:** Pawns advance through depth layers and promote on reaching the far face; castling is not used. Movement follows the 3D piece rules described in the in-game guide.

**Checked:** `node --check game.js` passed. In Chromium, I verified the board renders, a pawn’s cross-layer moves are indicated, a cross-layer move changes turns, and undo restores the position. Reviewed the latest screenshot at `/tmp/opencode/voxel-latest.jpg`.
